purpose: Closed-denominator adjudication and repair of Biome 2.5.1 useNamingConvention configuration. This is durable evidence, not an authority table or work tracker.

semantics: Custom conventions use first match within one convention array.
In Biome 2.5.1 an override's options.conventions REPLACES the global convention array; it does not append or inherit unlisted selectors.
Therefore every naming override is a self-contained array: sigil forwarding, path-specific key rows first, then the complete explicit code-owned selector matrix.
A match capture forwards only the captured text to the format check; the leading row preserves Biome's stock leading/trailing underscore and dollar allowance.

Named imports, destructured object properties, non-identifier members, ambient declarations, and override members are outside this rule's evidence plane. No computed or bracket syntax was introduced to evade the rule.

Fresh review showed that path overrides replaced this array and silently fell back to hidden defaults for omitted selectors; the final matrix adds explicit member ownership and duplicates all 21 code selectors into every override.

memberOwnership.reason: Global member defaults are explicit. Path arrays replace the global array, so their property rows may admit wire formats without shadowing or merge-order ambiguity.

semanticAdjudication.codeOwnedIdentifiers: The global rule and all nine path overrides explicitly carry the complete 21-row code selector matrix. The structural pin compares every override copy byte-for-byte at the row level, and the adversarial mutation proves an override-local variable cannot fall back to Biome defaults.
semanticAdjudication.externalWireAndSerializedKeys: Each replacement array puts its two path-local object/type property rows before the broad explicit member rows. Only those property selectors receive snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, or PascalCase; variables, functions, parameters, class members, and type names stay under the duplicated code matrix.
semanticAdjudication.computedSyntax: No source was rewritten to a computed or bracket key and no selector was avoided through syntax changes.

adversarialReplacementControl.meaning: Fails if an override omits the variable selector and falls back to hidden camelCase, if global key rows merge ahead of the path key row, or if property rows follow broad member rows.

confirmedRepairCandidates: Any future naming override must copy sigil forwarding plus all 21 code selector rows and put its narrow key rows first. The config pin is the synchronization control for this deliberate duplication.

overridePolicy.semantics: The nine arrays deliberately duplicate the code matrix because Biome 2.5.1 replaces options.conventions at an override boundary. Omitting even one selector delegates that selector to Biome's hidden stock default.
overridePolicy.ordering: Path-specific property rows precede broad typeMember and objectLiteralMember rows; otherwise first-match would make the wire formats unreachable.
overridePolicy.consolidation: Rows remain attached to their existing path overrides because their key formats, exact serialized exceptions, and adjacent non-naming rules differ. The duplication is explicit policy, not accidental copy drift; the structural pin compares every copy to the global code matrix.
